facts.text: Originally a farming community at Knowles Station, Kensington grew into a summer refuge for Washington residents escaping the capital's humidity.
The B&O Railroad's Metropolitan Branch crossed Rock Creek in 1873, turning the area into a rail hub that spurred growth.
In the early 1890s, developer Brainard Warner purchased land to build a planned Victorian community complete with church, library, and newspaper.
Kensington station on the MARC Brunswick Line connects downtown Kensington with Washington, D.C., and points west like Harpers Ferry.
The Noyes Library for Young Children, Montgomery County's oldest public library, sits in Kensington and serves families since 1905.
Warner named his development "Kensington Park," the tenth and largest subdivision in the area, reflecting his vision for a genteel community.
